# The Lights That Dance at the Edge

## Scripture

*"Where were you when I laid the earth's foundation? Tell me, if you understand. Who marked off its dimensions? Surely you know! Who stretched a measuring line across it? On what were its footings set, or who laid its cornerstone—while the morning stars sang together and all the angels shouted for joy?"* — Job 38:4–7 (NIV)

## Reflection

In the far northern skies, when solar winds collide with Earth's magnetic field, curtains of green and violet light ripple across the darkness. The aurora borealis—a dance of charged particles guided by invisible forces—appears without warning and vanishes just as quietly. No one can command it. No one can schedule it. It simply comes, and those who witness it stand breathless.

Job never saw the northern lights, yet God's questions to him echo the same wonder: *Where were you?* Before the first atom, before the first light, before the morning stars sang—God was there, laying foundations we cannot measure, stretching lines we cannot trace.

We spend so much of our lives trying to map what God has made, to predict, to control, to understand. But the aurora reminds us that creation still moves at the impulse of its Maker. There are glories we cannot summon, seasons we cannot force, and mysteries we cannot solve. And that is not a reason for fear—it is a reason for worship. The God who choreographs lights across the Arctic sky is the same God who holds your days in His hands.

You need not understand everything to trust the One who does.

## Prayer

Lord of the dancing lights and the singing stars, forgive us for demanding to understand what You have only asked us to behold. Thank You for the mysteries that keep us on our knees and the beauty that lifts our eyes. When we cannot trace Your hand, help us trust Your heart. Amen.
